title: Rome, crowns and castles
intro: From a famous murder in Rome to the end of the Middle Ages.

events.text: Julius Caesar is killed in Rome by a group of senators.
events.label: Caesar

events.text: The last emperor in the West, Romulus Augustulus, is removed. This is the usual date for the end of the Western Roman Empire.
events.label: Western Rome falls

events.text: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.
events.label: Charlemagne

events.text: William of Normandy wins the Battle of Hastings and becomes King of England.
events.label: Hastings

events.text: King John of England seals Magna Carta.
events.label: Magna Carta

events.text: The Hundred Years' War between England and France begins, as it is usually dated.
events.label: Hundred Years War

events.text: Constantinople falls to the Ottoman army of Sultan Mehmed II.
events.label: Constantinople

events.text: Columbus's first voyage reaches the Caribbean.
events.label: Columbus

events.text: Vasco da Gama's ships reach India by sea from Europe.
events.label: Vasco da Gama

events.text: The Victoria, the last ship of Magellan's expedition, returns to Spain after sailing around the world.
events.label: Around the world

events.text: The Mayflower reaches the coast of North America with settlers from England.
events.label: Mayflower

events.text: James Cook sails along the east coast of Australia and lands at Botany Bay.
events.label: Captain Cook

events.text: Roald Amundsen's party is the first to reach the South Pole.
events.label: South Pole

events.text: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay are the first known climbers to reach the top of Mount Everest.
events.label: Everest

title: Ideas that changed minds
intro: Faith, science and the big books.

events.text: Martin Luther publishes his Ninety-five Theses.
events.label: Luther

events.text: Copernicus publishes his book placing the Sun at the centre of the planets' paths.
events.label: Copernicus

events.text: Galileo sees four moons of Jupiter through his telescope.
events.label: Galileo

events.text: Isaac Newton publishes his Principia, setting out his laws of motion and gravity.
events.label: Newton

events.text: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species.
events.label: Darwin

events.text: Dmitri Mendeleev presents his periodic table of the elements.
events.label: Periodic table

events.text: Albert Einstein publishes his theory of special relativity.
events.label: Special relativity

events.text: The American colonies adopt the Declaration of Independence.
events.label: Declaration

events.text: The French Revolution begins; crowds storm the Bastille in Paris.
events.label: Bastille

events.text: Haiti declares independence, the first country led by formerly enslaved people to do so.
events.label: Haiti

events.text: Napoleon is defeated at the Battle of Waterloo.
events.label: Waterloo

events.text: The American Civil War begins with the firing on Fort Sumter.
events.label: Civil War

events.text: The German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles.
events.label: German Empire

events.text: Revolutions in Russia end the rule of the tsar and bring the Bolsheviks to power.
events.label: Russian Revolution

title: Two world wars and after
intro: From 1914 to the end of the Cold War era.

events.text: The First World War begins.
events.label: World War I

events.text: The armistice ends the fighting of the First World War.
events.label: Armistice

events.text: The Second World War begins in Europe.
events.label: World War II

events.text: The Second World War ends.
events.label: War ends

events.text: India becomes independent from British rule.
events.label: India independent

events.text: The Berlin Wall is opened.
events.label: Berlin Wall

events.text: The Soviet Union is dissolved.
events.label: Soviet Union

title: Rights and reforms
intro: People and laws that widened who counts.

events.text: The United Kingdom passes the Slavery Abolition Act.
events.label: Abolition Act

events.text: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country where women win the vote in national elections.
events.label: New Zealand women vote

events.text: The 19th Amendment gives women in the United States the right to vote.
events.label: 19th Amendment

events.text: The United Nations adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
events.label: Human Rights

events.text: A great crowd gathers at the March on Washington for jobs and freedom.
events.label: March on Washington

events.text: The Civil Rights Act becomes law in the United States.
events.label: Civil Rights Act

events.text: South Africa holds its first elections open to adults of every race.
events.label: South Africa votes

events.text: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens, the first intercity line run by steam trains.
events.label: Railway

events.text: Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone.
events.label: Telephone

events.text: Thomas Edison's team makes a long-lasting electric light bulb.
events.label: Light bulb

events.text: The ENIAC, an early general-purpose electronic computer, is unveiled in the United States.
events.label: ENIAC

events.text: The first message is sent over ARPANET, an early computer network.
events.label: ARPANET

events.text: Intel releases the 4004, the first commercial microprocessor.
events.label: Microprocessor

events.text: The World Wide Web is announced to the public.
events.label: World Wide Web

events.text: Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein is published.
events.label: Frankenstein

events.text: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is first performed in Vienna.
events.label: Beethoven's Ninth

events.text: The Great Exhibition opens in the Crystal Palace in London.
events.label: Great Exhibition

events.text: The Eiffel Tower opens in Paris for the World's Fair.
events.label: Eiffel Tower

events.text: Stravinsky's ballet The Rite of Spring has its first performance in Paris, and the crowd is noisy.
events.label: Rite of Spring

events.text: The Empire State Building opens in New York.
events.label: Empire State

events.text: Pablo Picasso paints Guernica, a huge picture about a bombed town.
events.label: Guernica

events.text: The Suez Canal opens, joining the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
events.label: Suez Canal

events.text: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated in New York Harbor.
events.label: Statue of Liberty

events.text: The first modern Olympic Games are held in Athens.
events.label: First Olympics

events.text: The Titanic sinks on her first voyage.
events.label: Titanic

events.text: The Panama Canal opens to ships.
events.label: Panama Canal

events.text: The first football World Cup is played, in Uruguay.
events.label: First World Cup

events.text: Roger Bannister runs the first mile in under four minutes.
events.label: Four-minute mile
